title: Shanghai's Nanjing Building digital twin (Huangpu District with Huawei) alerts a guard to an opened third-floor window; a sensor, not AI, detected it and the anecdote carries three dates
summary: A Huawei-hosted launch on 25 Feb 2021 presented a window-opening alert sent to a guard's wristband. Knews and Jiefang Daily say that a window sensor detected it; the story is retold with three dates.
account: The OECD AI Incidents entry says Shanghai, with Huawei, launched an AI-powered digital twin in the Nanjing Building. It says the twin “detected a high-risk behavior (open window), alerted security, and enabled immediate intervention”. The anecdote appears in Eastday (reporter Xue Ningwei, 25 Feb 2021, via Sohu). During Spring Festival a customer on the third floor opened a window and held a phone out to photograph Nanjing Road. A guard arrived to stop it. Eastday says how the guard knew was “revealed at today's launch”, the “Shanghai city minimum management unit digital governance” release. It was held at the Huangpu District city operations center, hosted by Huawei Technologies per smartcity.team (1 Mar 2021). Jiefang Daily (7 May 2021, via GMW) retells the same window scene during the May Day holiday, naming guard Fan Tianyu. Banyuetan/Xinhua (reporter Zhou Lin, 6 Jul 2021, via The Paper) retells it during the Dragon Boat holiday with the same guard and wording. No single date can be fixed. The Cyberspace Administration of China repost (4 Mar 2021) phrases it conditionally (“if a visitor opens a window...”). The only witnessed detection was a Knews reporter's deliberate “open window” test at the launch. Huawei engineer Chen Tao also simulated smoking there for the camera algorithm. Both Knews and Jiefang Daily say a window-mounted sensor detected the opening and pushed an alert to the guard's wristband through the digital twin. The AI algorithms described (20-plus per Knews and Jiefang Daily, 50-plus per Eastday) run on the 170-plus cameras for smoking, crowd flow and bike parking. Jiefang Daily reports 995 door/window alerts from January to May 2021. An official attributed more than 80% of handled events across the system to visitors testing the devices; the report does not give that percentage specifically for windows. The building is Huawei's flagship store. No harm occurred and no beneficiary is identifiable. The deployment itself is well documented (Huangpu District and Huawei, built January 2021; 17 device categories, 80-plus sensor sets, 170-plus cameras). No English-language report was found, and the China Central Television (CCTV-2) segment is not among the sources. The system's zhiding.cn copy is marked “industry-supplied copy”.
purpose: The digital twin was built to monitor the building's “vital signs” (vibration, smoke, lifts, crowd flow, open windows) and push alerts to staff. Window opening was named at the launch as a falling-object risk the system flags.
system: Nanjing Building 1:1 'living' digital twin on Huawei Cloud: 80-plus IoT sensor sets in 17 categories, 170-plus cameras, and 20-plus (Knews, Jiefang Daily) or 50-plus (Eastday) AI algorithms for smoking, crowd-flow and parking detection

fields.account: The OECD AI Incidents entry says Shanghai, with Huawei, launched an AI-powered digital twin in the Nanjing Building. It says the twin “detected a high-risk behavior (open window), alerted security, and enabled immediate intervention”. The anecdote appears in Eastday (reporter Xue Ningwei, 25 Feb 2021, via Sohu). During Spring Festival a customer on the third floor opened a window and held a phone out to photograph Nanjing Road. A guard arrived to stop it. Eastday says how the guard knew was “revealed at today's launch”, the “Shanghai city minimum management unit digital governance” release. It was held at the Huangpu District city operations center, hosted by Huawei Technologies per smartcity.team (1 Mar 2021). Jiefang Daily (7 May 2021, via GMW) retells the same window scene during the May Day holiday, naming guard Fan Tianyu. Banyuetan/Xinhua (reporter Zhou Lin, 6 Jul 2021, via The Paper) retells it during the Dragon Boat holiday with the same guard and wording. No single date can be fixed. The Cyberspace Administration of China repost (4 Mar 2021) phrases it conditionally (“if a visitor opens a window...”). The only witnessed detection was a Knews reporter's deliberate “open window” test at the launch. Huawei engineer Chen Tao also simulated smoking there for the camera algorithm. Both Knews and Jiefang Daily say a window-mounted sensor detected the opening and pushed an alert to the guard's wristband through the digital twin. The AI algorithms described (20-plus per Knews and Jiefang Daily, 50-plus per Eastday) run on the 170-plus cameras for smoking, crowd flow and bike parking. Jiefang Daily reports 995 door/window alerts from January to May 2021. An official attributed more than 80% of handled events across the system to visitors testing the devices; the report does not give that percentage specifically for windows. The building is Huawei's flagship store. No harm occurred and no beneficiary is identifiable. The deployment itself is well documented (Huangpu District and Huawei, built January 2021; 17 device categories, 80-plus sensor sets, 170-plus cameras). No English-language report was found, and the China Central Television (CCTV-2) segment is not among the sources. The system's zhiding.cn copy is marked “industry-supplied copy”.

fields.account: The OECD AI Incidents entry says Shanghai, with Huawei, launched an AI-powered digital twin in the Nanjing Building. It says the twin “detected a high-risk behavior (open window), alerted security, and enabled immediate intervention”. The anecdote appears in Eastday (reporter Xue Ningwei, 25 Feb 2021, via Sohu). During Spring Festival a customer on the third floor opened a window and held a phone out to photograph Nanjing Road. A guard arrived to stop it. Eastday says how the guard knew was “revealed at today's launch”, the “Shanghai city minimum management unit digital governance” release. It was held at the Huangpu District city operations center, hosted by Huawei Technologies per smartcity.team (1 Mar 2021). Jiefang Daily (7 May 2021, via GMW) retells the same window scene during the May Day holiday, naming guard Fan Tianyu. Banyuetan/Xinhua (reporter Zhou Lin, 6 Jul 2021, via The Paper) retells it during the Dragon Boat holiday with the same guard and wording. No single date can be fixed. The Cyberspace Administration of China repost (4 Mar 2021) phrases it conditionally (“if a visitor opens a window...”). The only witnessed detection was a Knews reporter's deliberate “open window” test at the launch. Huawei engineer Chen Tao also simulated smoking there for the camera algorithm. Both Knews and Jiefang Daily say a window-mounted sensor detected the opening and pushed an alert to the guard's wristband through the digital twin. The AI algorithms described (20-plus per Knews and Jiefang Daily, 50-plus per Eastday) run on the 170-plus cameras for smoking, crowd flow and bike parking. Jiefang Daily reports 995 door/window alerts from January to May 2021. An official attributed more than 80% of handled events across the system to visitors testing the devices; the report does not give that percentage specifically for windows. The building is Huawei's flagship store. No harm occurred and no beneficiary is identifiable. The deployment itself is well documented (Huangpu District and Huawei, built January 2021; 17 device categories, 80-plus sensor sets, 170-plus cameras). No English-language report was found, and the China Central Television (CCTV-2) segment is not among the sources. The system's zhiding.cn copy is marked “industry-supplied copy”.
